commits.summary: Close the engine-priorities loop's open work: the Python test failures fixed, the own checker's encoding timed whole per word-level operation, the rest deferred as findings, and a draft brief for JBMC's upstream defects (verification pending)
commits.body:
test_build.py's 35 errors (KeyError: 'verdict' and the like) were tests that read committed results raw, as if all were format 1. 28 are now stored as format 2, so these tests read them through result_format.load, the documented way back to the flat view. Two tests rested on results recorded before the model-contract connection, and 076 and 072 were run again since (jobs 20261106-1811xx): test_a_result_recorded_before_the_connection_renders_as_before now reads 077, the same breaker, still recorded that way, and test_format_two_stores_each_fact_once expects 072's two kinds of obligation, configurations and the operator's contract, which checks more than before. test_performance.py's one failure, test_the_exporter_stops_at_the_first_failure, passed only on a machine with Langfuse configured (here llm-dlc/infra/langfuse/.env is absent, so langfuse_send raised before the mocked exporter). It now stubs the configuration and the project directory, as another test in the file does. Both suites pass: test_build 161, test_performance 102.

The own checker's encoding phase (lib/src/bmc/bits.rs) timed one operation in 64 at random and counted it 64 times. Single gates (nanoseconds) and whole word-level circuits (a 32-bit multiplier is thousands of gates) came from one sampling stream, and its seed is fixed, so a short run that sampled one large circuit counted it 64 times on every run. Its encoding plus solving then passed the run's own time and it was flagged phasesExcess: real/checksum/broken-property in job 20261106-201041, and example 018's proof in jobs -231837 and -000039. Now each word-level operation is timed whole, and only single gates are sampled. Reproducer first: the_encoding_estimate_does_not_count_a_large_circuit_many_times_over puts one multiplication among 256 cheap gates at every position. Before the change, the multiplication at operation 74 was estimated at 0.063 s of 0.001 s. After it, every position is within the phases' tolerance, in 6 runs. lib/benchmark/README.md's encoding row says so. Rust: unit 180 and conformance 9 (2 ignored) pass. Integration had 63 of 64 pass: the_tools_own_checker_agrees_with_jbmc_on_integer_proofs failed at Pricing#total's own-checker proof after 611 s, the known wall-clock flake (VF-010), and passed alone in 12.7 s.

Job 20261107-032249-the-own-checker-s-encoding-timed-whole-p reruns the benchmark's own-checker runs at this commit. It checks that none is flagged (job -201041 flagged 1 of 356), and that timing each word-level operation made the runs no slower, by the median ratio of seconds to -201041's over runs of 0.1 s or more (at most 1.10). The compare step was dry-run on the committed results.

Job 20261107-024759 came back passed (collected by the runner in the previous commit). 071's first two proofs are verified under strict with no gap, 013 has no JBMC gap, and the corpus agrees under JBMC and auto. VF-005 is closed in verification/findings.md, and with it Phase 5's last criterion. 071's and 013's notes record the run, and their pages were re-rendered. VF-008, closed earlier but listed under Open, moves to the closed section.

Deferred by the user's decision, until after the foundations loop, as findings: VF-010, the own checker's branch probes depending on wall-clock time (Pricing#total); VF-011, the unwinding bound counted over a whole path rather than per entry of a loop (example 052), not yet reproduced; and VF-009, kept open and untriaged. VF-009 is also all that is left of the native stream's step 3 conformance job: those cases passed under JBMC and auto in jobs -012013 and -022319, and only --confirm fails, on boomTwice and enumBroken.

llm-dlc/loops/jbmc-upstream.md (new) is a draft brief, not approved, for the three JBMC defects the loop found and drafted reports for: a returned value computed after the try range, unmasked right shifts, and extra class initializers. It makes each report ready for the user to file, every claim backed by a job log of the report's own example on the JVM and on stock JBMC. It also adds a job that says whether a given JBMC version is fixed, before any guard is lifted, and leaves the user four decisions (network access, a patch, which findings join). Cause 4's report now has its evidence: job -010728's step 3 gives VERIFICATION FAILED on both of I.java's methods. engine-priorities.md's Progress records all of this; its status is waiting on job -032249. The rest of the brief is as it was.
